$comment: Syntax Download Manager — performance budgets (Phase 22). Single source of truth consumed by scripts/check-budgets.mjs (build gate, runs after the renderer build) and by vitest perf tests. Every budget carries the sandbox-measured baseline it was calibrated from. Values are honest ceilings with headroom for CI noise; they exist to catch pathological regressions, not to be rubber-stamped.
environment: Linux sandbox, debug (dev) profile Rust build, Node 24, release-mode vite bundle

coldStartReadyMs.note: spawn -> core.ready over the real binary; debug profile. Release is faster. Catches blocking startup work (sync I/O on the boot path, accidental await-on-init).

rssAfterReadyKb.note: VmRSS after the first ready transition (unix /proc sampling; Windows checked user-side via Diagnostics). ~4x headroom over a booted core.

echoAvgUs.note: average core.ping round-trip over the spawned binary (write + read + JSONL parse), 100 samples. ~20x headroom; catches per-request sync work or double parsing.

maxTotalJsBytes.note: sum of all .js assets in dist/renderer/assets (sourcemaps excluded). ~11.6% headroom over the Phase 22 baseline; catches new heavyweight deps or accidental double imports.

maxLargestChunkBytes.note: largest single .js asset. A future code split must not grow any chunk past the total-bytes budget of today.

maxTotalCssBytes.note: sum of all .css assets (Fluent v9 styles are runtime-injected today, hence 0). Future CSS must not silently balloon.

ipcDispatch2000Ms.note: wall-clock for 2000 fully validated IpcRouter.dispatch round-trips (envelope + params + result zod schemas). Observed 3.6 us/op in vitest; the 0.5 ms/op ceiling (~140x headroom) exists to catch pathological per-request work, not noise.

uiStoreHotPathMs.note: 2000 upsertJob + 2000 patchProgress over a 200-job list (the downloads-page hot path). Observed 41.5 ms; ~24x headroom.

uiQueueSortMs.note: 100 compareQueueDisplay sorts of a 500-job list. Observed 6.1 ms; ~80x headroom.
